limitations: Numerical verification of a synthetic, internally consistent model only. Nothing here is empirical validation, a simulator benchmark result, or evidence about any real chemistry (plan §3.1-3.2).

The oracle and reference values share the SYN-001 thermodynamic definitions with the future K02 provider; agreement between them will verify algebra and bookkeeping, not enthalpy or K-value data (blueprint A09).

The reference values were produced by Fable and the oracle by Opus from the same plan §3.1 definitions; the two implementations are independent in code (mpmath at 40 digits vs pure-Python double precision) but not independent in authorship of the underlying equations, which are the plan's.

D08 and A04 are contributed to, not closed: no property provider, unit model, or real-provider conformance exists (K02, M01); no executable ensemble generator or saved draws exist (T06). Requirement statuses remain planned.

The Protocol classes of plan §2.1 are frozen as a document (docs/interfaces-frozen.md), not yet as Python typing.Protocol objects; those are introduced by P02/K02/K06 and must match the document verbatim.

docs/derivations/scripts/fable_verify_oracle.py was run against this commit and is committed together with this manifest (the following commit), per the evidence convention that the manifest commit follows the code commit.
Single platform (Debian 13, x86-64, CPython 3.13.5); no CI run has executed.

The A.1 finite-difference specification error (see identity.fd_check_a1) was Fable's; it was found by Opus, reported rather than worked around, and corrected in the specification. The identity itself was never in doubt: it is verified at 40 digits.
